 Judgment

The claimant in LAC No.108/2010 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi, is aggrieved by the Order of the Reference Court which is declined to award interest on the compensation awarded for the period between the date of dispossession and the date of 4(1)
notification under the Land Acquisition the Act 1984.
The matter lies in a narrow compass.

2. There is no dispute that on 12.07.2007 Section 4(1) notification under the Land Acquisition Act,
1984 was published to acquire the petitioner's land bearing Sy.No.161.
The land is acquired to construct a check dam.
The claimant sought reference being dissatisfied with the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
The Reference Court declined to award interest from the date of dispossession though the dispossession has taken place prior to Section 4(1) notification.
Appellants claim interest on the compensation awarded from the date of dispossession till Section 4(1) notification.

The learned counsel for the appellant in support of his submission submit that the appellants are entitled to interest by way of damages from the date of dispossession till Section 4(1) notification and relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case Madishetti Bala Ramul (dead)By Lrs. V.Land Acquisition Officer reported in 2007 (9) SCC 650.
4.
By referring to the said judgment, he would urge that in this case, the date of dispossession prior to Section 4(1) notification is established.
No compensation is awarded for the illegal dispossession.
No interest is awarded from the date of dispossession till Section 4(1) notification.
Thus, he would urge that the Reference Court erred in declining the interest for the said period.

5. The learned Government Advocate opposing appeal would submit that the appellants are not entitled to interest from the date of dispossession till the date of Section 4(1) notification and remedy if any for the appellants are to file an application before the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10803 Jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner and should seek damages.
6.

The learned Government Advocate has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case R.L. Jain (D) By LRS. Vs. D.D.A. and Others reported in AIR 2004 SC 1904.
7.

entities.text: R.L. Jain (D) By LRS. Vs. D.D.A. and Others reported in AIR 2004 SC 1904
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has considered the contentions raised at the Bar.

8. In terms of the order passed by this Court, the learned Government Advocate has also filed a memo before this Court and in terms of the letter dated 10.02.2009 annexed to the said memo, it is apparent that the possession of the land is taken on 30.03.1999.

Admittedly, Section 4(1)
notification is issued on 12.07.2007.

Thus, it is evident that possession is taken before Section 4(1)
notification.
The law does not contemplate dispossession of the owner of the land before issuance of Section 4(1) notification.
Thus, the State has NC: 2023:KHC-D:10803 illegally taken the possession of the property from the land owner.

sentences.text: 4 9. At this juncture, it is relevant to refer to Article 300A of Constitution of India.
Right to property is a constitutional right.
Article 300A contemplates that no person shall be deprived of his property otherwise than in accordance with law.
10. The course open for the State was to acquire the land of the appellant in case the land was acquired for building a check dam.
After issuing Section 4(1) notification and following all other procedures, the land ought to have been acquired.
However, in 1998 itself, the State has dispossessed the appellant and the land acquisition proceeding is initiated in the year 2007.

Thus,
for 9 years, the land owner is deprived of possession of the property and he was not awarded any compensation.
In this context, the appellants are before this Court.

11. It is also relevant to note that when the appellant was dispossessed and the respondent-State NC:
2023:KHC-D:10803 started putting up the check dam in the land belonging to the appellant, the suit is filed before the Principal Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Jamkhandi, in O.S.No.224/1999.
The appellant sought restraint order against the respondent from putting up any structure in the property belonging to the appellant and also sought mandatory injunction.
On 09.03.2005, the suit is decreed.
The permanent injunction is granted as well as the mandatory injunction is granted directing the defendant-State to remove the check dam.
However, the decree is not put in execution.
The appellant has chosen to claim the compensation.

12. It is also required to be noticed in the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, after noticing the fact that the possession of the properties taken prior to Section 4(1) notification, the Special Land Acquisition Officer himself has observed in the award that the appellants are entitled to seek appropriate relief in respect of dispossession prior to Section 4(1) notification.
Though the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of R.L. Jain referred to supra has held that remedy of the appellants are to approach the Deputy Commissioner seeking damages

, in the case of Madishetti Bala Ramul referred supra, the Hon'ble Apex Court has awarded interest from the date of dispossession till the date of 4(1) notification at the rate of 15% p.a.
14.

In the light of facts and circumstances narrated above, this Court is of the view that it is not appropriate to drive the appellant to one more round of litigation to seek damages from the respondent-State.

Since the date of dispossession is very much established from the documents dated 10.02.2009 referred to above, it is apparent that the appellant was dispossessed on 30.03.1999 and he is entitled to interest by way of damages at the rate of 9% p.a. for the first year of dispossession and thereafter, from 30.3.2000 till the date of Section 4(1) notification i.e., till 12.07.2007 at the rate of 15% p.a. on the compensation awarded by the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10803 Reference Court in LAC No.108/2010 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award dated 18.11.2016 passed in LAC No.108/2010 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi, are modified.

iii) Appellants are entitled to interest @ 9% p.a. for the first year of dispossession i.e., from 30.03.1999, till 29.03.2000 and thereafter, at the rate of 15% p.a. till the date of Section 4(1)
notification i.e., till 12.07.2007 by way of damages on the compensation awarded by the Reference Court in LAC No.108/2010 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi.
